subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core agent teleconference lifecycle primitive now, and if so what storage, transcript, authorization, and handoff boundaries must the first PR use?
rationale: The feature is concrete and useful, but it adds core CLI/API surface plus durable cross-agent state and sensitive transcript behavior that cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Sponsor A Scoped Core Design
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a narrow design/PR that uses approved storage, reuses existing identity.emoji, defines transcript retention/redaction, and composes with the sessions_send handoff contract.

options.title: Route To Plugin/ClawHub First
options.body: Treat the visible meeting loop as optional orchestration and require a plugin/package path until a missing core API is proven.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Multi-Agent Work
options.body: Close or defer this specific lifecycle track in favor of the broader multi-agent collaboration RFC and handoff-acknowledgement PR once maintainers choose that architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor A Scoped Core Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a narrow design/PR that uses approved storage, reuses existing identity.emoji, defines transcript retention/redaction, and composes with the sessions_send handoff contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer-facing scoping comment on this issue and has recent adjacent sessions/A2A/storage history.
